I’ll use gpt-6-astra at xhigh for the evidence review and keep all work offline. I’ll read the recorded run and reference files, then write only the two requested review files; recovery status will come only from the recorded journal.

I’m applying the xts-board-evidence skill to preserve the raw results and their limits. The IDF reference uses separately labelled 0–30-second receiver bytes, so this review will keep those derived rates separate from native summaries and assess UDP quality independently.

All four receivers have 30 contiguous one-second rows. Their derived 0–30-second rates are TCP RX **4.280820**, TCP TX **7.582583**, UDP RX **9.991688**, and UDP TX **8.965824 Mbit/s**. The journal records verified restore writes but a pending full comparison, so restoration remains unconfirmed.

Both TCP endpoint totals agree. UDP RX remains the main deficit: **52.397% native sequence gaps**, 241 out-of-order packets, and a missing final ACK. UDP TX has 11 gaps out of 22,930 and an explicit ACK; its rate is within the IDF reference range but below its mean. This supports a TCP-window-only 32k A/B while retaining IOB256.

The captured host streams match the actual owned-worker logs and all eight receipt hashes. The E87 kernel/AppFS payload hashes and recorded install readbacks also match. The review will retain the PHY/power-save and reporting limits, and record that this is one diagnostic round, with no E88 performance or xTS acceptance claim.

The UDP RX snapshots show 3,477 IOB preallocation drops, 1,008 additional queue-entry drops, and 11,324 UDP stack drops. IOBs return to 256 free afterward, but there is no traffic-time IOB peak measurement. These records support deferring a global pool cut while UDP RX service is investigated.

The actual journal now records `original_restored_full_flash_verified`, with `full_byte_compare: true` at **10:25:19 UTC**. The report can therefore record verified restoration; that status comes from the completed journal entry.
